channel.title: ConnectorZone guides
channel.description: Practical guides to Model Context Protocol connectors, clients and configuration.

item.title: How to choose an MCP connector
item.description: A working method for choosing between thousands of Model Context Protocol connectors, using provenance, transport, credential shape and published references rather than popularity.

item.title: A security review for MCP connectors
item.description: A practical security review for Model Context Protocol connectors, covering trust boundaries, credential scope, prompt injection through tool results and what registry listing really certifies.

item.title: Local servers or hosted endpoints
item.description: A comparison of local stdio MCP servers and hosted HTTP endpoints, covering latency, credentials, client support, data flow and the cases where only one option works.

item.title: OAuth and authorisation in MCP
item.description: A working explanation of the MCP authorisation model for HTTP servers, covering scoped consent, token storage, revocation and the difference between an authorisation flow and a pasted API key.

item.title: Configuring MCP in every major client
item.description: A cross client reference for Model Context Protocol configuration, covering file locations, key names, transport fields and the copy paste errors that silently break a server.

item.title: What the 2026-07-28 protocol revision changes
item.description: A practical read of the 2026-07-28 Model Context Protocol specification revision, what it means for connector authors and operators, and how to check that a client and server agree.

item.title: Debugging a connector that will not load
item.description: A step by step method for debugging Model Context Protocol servers that fail to load, report zero tools or disappear after a client update.

item.title: Reading provenance in the MCP registry
item.description: How to read publisher provenance in the official MCP Registry, including namespace verification, bulk submissions, duplicate descriptions and the limits of any registry signal.
